title: Canadian teenager and her favourite cow win a top dairy prize
summary:
Some competitions have tennis rackets. This one has cows! At the World Dairy Expo in Madison, Wisconsin, a Canadian teenager celebrated a big win with her favourite cow on Sunday.

Alyson Doiron is a 16-year-old high school student from Cap-Santé in Quebec. Her favourite cow, Arolene Dempsey Ella, is usually called Ella. The five-year-old cow won the top prize at the International Junior Holstein Show. Holstein is a breed, or type, of dairy cow.

Doiron cheered and cried when she accepted the honour for Ella. She said the cow is easy to work with and much loved. The prize mattered to her, and she felt it showed the strength of cow showing in Quebec.

The Expo brings together people from around the world. However, health and safety rules mean the animals competing come from Canadian and American farms.

A major win can increase a cow's value by tens of thousands of dollars. It can also make the cow's future calves more valuable.

Getting there takes planning. Brian Carscadden and his team from a Quebec dairy company drove more than 1,500 kilometres with 25 cows in trailers.

The event took place during a trade dispute between Canada and the United States. Carscadden said his business had not been affected yet and that the dispute did not come up often in conversations at the Expo.
